headline: 情歌陪他走出憂鬱
context: 一位音樂圈工作者投書《衛報》，說創作歌手 Raye 的歌曲〈I Know You're Hurting〉，讓他第一次真正聽懂歌詞裡在說什麼，也因此正視自己多年來一直迴避的憂鬱狀態。他形容自己有次在車上聽這首歌聽到哭，那是這首歌真正「被聽見」的一刻。

sources.name: The Guardian
sources.summary: I had always ignored my anguished mental state or tried to push it aside, and CBT didn’t work for me – then one song seemed to articulate my pain Six months ago, I was driving past John Lewis on the M40 with my wife and stepdaughter, Raye’s I Know You’re Hurting playing on the stereo, when I realised I was crying. It was the third time I’d listened to the song, but it was the first time I’d really heard it. It was as though the lyrics were speaking directly to me: “I can see you standing on the edge … You give when you have little left to give.” Music had made me emotional before, but only ever because of the melody or the arrangement or the orchestration. I have worked in music since I was 21, and as a recording and mix engineer, I’ll listen to a song all day, taking it apart to work out how to make it better. After listening to a song 200 times, it inevitably loses its meaning, and over the years, I’ve become desensitised to the power music can have. But this time, for the first time, it was the lyrics that brought me to tears. Continue reading...
sources.title: Raye’s I Know You’re Hurting urged me to confront a lifetime of depression

voice_text: 一位長年在音樂圈工作的人，投書談到自己的憂鬱。他說，Raye 的歌曲〈I Know You're Hurting〉，是他第一次真正聽懂歌詞在說什麼的一次。以前他總是迴避自己的低潮，這首歌卻讓他停下來，正視多年來一直沒面對的狀態。
